strengths: Well-motivated problem: Improving LLM reliability and confidence calibration is critical for real-world deployment
Clear conceptual contribution: 'reasoning-primary, information-secondary' paradigm offers a principled alternative to information-heavy RAG
Principled algorithmic approach: Using constrained RL with Lagrangian optimization is theoretically grounded for multi-objective optimization
Comprehensive evaluation: Five knowledge-intensive benchmarks including real-world Google Search API scenarios
Appropriate evaluation metrics: Measures reliability and false-certain rate alongside accuracy to assess trustworthiness
Ablation study present: Demonstrates value of adaptive λ adjustment versus fixed penalty weights
weaknesses: Incomplete submission: Abstract states 'This paper will be continuously updated'; Table 1 has incomplete rows; only 7 pages suggesting preliminary work—unacceptable for peer review
Confidence extraction mechanism unexplained: How is c(st) ∈ {1,...,10} computed? From model outputs, learned separately, or extracted from logits? Fundamental detail missing
Reward function notation unclear (Eq. 6): Meaning of 'rf_final = rformat(0.1 rformat + 0.9 racc + λ rreliab)' is ambiguous; unclear if multiplication by rformat is intended or typo
Reliability reward non-differentiability unaddressed (Eq. 5): Boolean formula combining logical operators; how is gradient computed? Straight-through estimators? Gumbel-softmax? Not specified
Unfair baseline comparisons: Unclear if all baselines use identical retrieval setup; some models may not use search at all, making comparison questionable
Incomplete training specification: Section 3.2 states 'subset of five benchmarks' but doesn't specify which; essential reproducibility information missing
No statistical significance testing: No error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests; unclear if improvements exceed noise
Missing important baselines: No comparison with standard calibration methods (temperature scaling, Platt scaling) or alternative constrained RL algorithms

Suspicious empirical results: False-certain rates of 0.01-0.02 unrealistically low; reliability consistently 0.75 across diverse models suspicious; high variance in accuracy (0.15-0.62) across benchmarks unexplained
Hyperparameter choices unjustified: Confidence threshold ζ=5, constraint threshold a=0.9, weight coefficients (0.1, 0.9)—no justification, sensitivity analysis, or ablation
Limited ablation studies: Only λ scheduling versus fixed λ compared; missing ablations on threshold ζ, reward weights, action space, verifier quality
No qualitative analysis: Missing example trajectories, failure case analysis, or discussion of when calibration helps versus hurts
Verifier reliability unaddressed: Which LLM verifier used? How reliable? Error propagation not discussed
Insufficient novelty: Extending GRPO with Lagrangian constraints is straightforward application of existing theory; technical contribution incremental
Missing computational analysis: No discussion of inference time costs with search or training duration
Presentation deficiencies: Typo 'ennumerate', inconsistent notation, no dedicated related work section, Figure 1 quality poor, missing discussion of limitations
Generalization claims weakly supported: Claims cross-task generalization but shows high variance; evidence insufficient

strengths: Addresses the important problem of LLM reliability and confidence calibration
Theoretically grounded constrained RL formulation based on established Lagrangian methods
Comprehensive evaluation across 5 benchmarks and multiple model sizes (7B, 70B, closed-source)
Includes ablation study comparing adaptive vs. fixed Lagrangian coefficient
Real-world evaluation using live Google Search API on recent benchmarks
weaknesses: Paper is explicitly incomplete: abstract states 'This paper will be continuously updated' with missing experimental details and incomplete sentences
Limited algorithmic novelty: straightforward application of existing constrained RL methods (Paternain et al. 2022, Tessler et al. 2018) with incremental GRPO extension

Critical methodological clarity issues: confidence score generation mechanism unexplained, frozen LLM verifier not specified, search query formulation absent, arbitrary threshold choices (ζ=5) unjustified
Weak calibration evaluation: reports only narrow binary 'reliability' metric (Eq. 5) without standard calibration measures (ECE, MCE, Brier score, calibration curves)
Suspicious experimental results: Deliberative Searcher achieves 0.01 false-certain rate on 0.35 accuracy, suggesting overfitting to metric rather than genuine calibration learning
Incomplete experimental setup: missing training dataset sizes, convergence criteria, batch size details, unclear baseline implementations (R1-Searcher, ReSearch not standard methods)
Weak ablation study: only ablates λ parameter; missing ablations of reward components, confidence threshold ζ, constraint threshold a, and search impact
No statistical significance testing: single point estimates without confidence intervals or error bars
Reproducibility failures: verifier model unspecified, knowledge cutoff unknown, search API behavior non-deterministic, confidence generation mechanism unexplained
Limited scope: only QA tasks evaluated; no comparison with standard calibration methods (temperature scaling, Platt scaling); no computational cost analysis

strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear positioning: the distinction between information-primary and reasoning-primary paradigms is intuitive and addresses the important challenge of LLM reliability and miscalibration

Principled constrained RL approach: sound mathematical formulation extending GRPO with Lagrangian penalties for reliability, building appropriately on established work (Paternain et al. 2022, Tessler et al. 2018)
Strong empirical results: consistent 0.75 reliability across model sizes (7B and 72B) with notably low false-certain rates (0.02-0.09) outperforming baselines across five benchmarks
Comprehensive evaluation: tested across five knowledge-intensive benchmarks, three model scales (7B, 70B, closed-source), and three metrics (accuracy, reliability, false-certain rate)
Helpful ablation study (Figure 1): demonstrates adaptive λ scheduling outperforms fixed-λ baseline with ~10% accuracy advantage and stable reliability trajectory
weaknesses: Critical submission readiness issue: manuscript explicitly states 'This paper will be continuously updated,' indicating it is an incomplete draft lacking related work section, discussion section, and analysis—not appropriate for conference submission

Severe reproducibility gaps: base model architectures unspecified, training data subset and splits undefined, search/read mechanisms underspecified (query formulation, retrieval ranking, stopping criteria unclear), verifier LLM identity undisclosed, hyperparameter choices appear arbitrary (α=1e-6, β=1e-3, η=0.1, ζ=5, λ₀=0.01 lack justification)

Oversimplified reliability metric: binary threshold-based definition (Eq. 5 with ζ=5) differs substantially from standard calibration measures (ECE, MCE, Brier score); no sensitivity analysis for threshold choice; essentially checks (correct AND confident) OR (wrong AND uncertain) without nuance

Limited technical novelty: core contribution applies existing constrained RL (Paternain et al. 2022) and GRPO (Shao et al. 2024) to QA with simple confidence thresholding; confidence calibration via reward shaping is not novel; lacks comparison with other calibration methods (temperature scaling, Platt scaling, etc.)

Incomplete and inconsistent experimental reporting: Table 1 bottom row (Deliberative Searcher-Deepseek-70b) truncated, 'Avg.' columns don't match simple column averages, no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals, baseline model names unclear

Limited scope and generalization: all evaluation on QA tasks only; approach assumes ground-truth references limiting applicability; no out-of-distribution or adversarial evaluation; unclear how reasoning-primary paradigm extends to non-QA domains

Missing error analysis and failure modes: no examples of successful vs. failed chains, no discussion of when/why method fails, no categorization of failure types, no analysis of search efficiency (average SEARCH/READ operations per question, latency compared to non-searching baselines)

Insufficient baseline coverage: inspired by OpenAI-o1 and DeepSeek-R1 but doesn't evaluate against them; limited discussion of recent calibration literature and agent-based QA systems; missing comparisons with other uncertainty estimation methods

strengths: Addresses important practical problem of LLM miscalibration with clear motivation and well-designed framework (2×2 False&Certain categorization)

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 5 benchmarks (both in-distribution and real-world OOD), multiple model scales (7B/72B/70B), and thorough ablations isolating retrieval quality from confidence calibration
Strong empirical results with 96% reduction in false-certain rates (54%→2% for 7B) while maintaining/improving accuracy across all benchmarks
Sound technical approach using principled constrained RL with adaptive Lagrangian multipliers that avoids expensive hyperparameter search
Excellent reproducibility with detailed hyperparameters, training prompts, computational resources, and implementation details in appendices
Demonstrates practical value: 4× inference compute savings through confidence-weighted aggregation vs majority voting at equivalent accuracy
Well-designed two-stage retrieval mechanism creates useful training signals through explicit relevance decisions
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: constrained RL formulation from Paternain et al. (2023); confidence-weighted aggregation from Taubenfeld et al. (2025); application to search-augmented QA is primarily engineering rather than methodological innovation

Oversimplified calibration metric: binary reliability threshold at ζ=5 on 0-10 scale is crude compared to standard measures (ECE, MCE, Brier score); lacks sensitivity analysis on threshold choice; masks calibration across confidence spectrum; claiming 'calibrated confidence' based on this metric is imprecise

Reward design lacks justification: weights in Eq. 6 (0.1/0.9 split) appear arbitrary with no ablation study; hard-threshold reliability (Eq. 5) is brittle; no comparison to continuous calibration loss alternatives despite mentioning ECE variant only in table

Concerning out-of-distribution performance: accuracy drops sharply on real-world search (GAIA/xbench-deepsearch: 0.15-0.35 for 7B model); despite improved calibration, low absolute accuracy undermines deployment claims; limited analysis of accuracy degradation

Evaluation design issues: (1) LLM-as-Judge using Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct may bias results toward models from same family; (2) multimodal architectures (Qwen2.5-VL) used but only text-based reasoning evaluated, incomplete validation of model choice; (3) missing comparisons to other adaptive sampling strategies

Intermediate confidence unused (acknowledged): models generate step-wise confidence but only final answer is optimized; represents missed opportunity for improved calibration throughout reasoning trajectory
Computational requirements are substantial (64 A100 GPUs × 60 hours for 72B), limiting reproducibility despite acknowledged accessibility of 7B variant
Limited error analysis: beyond single case study (Figure 4), minimal investigation of when calibration succeeds/fails, performance variance across question types, or question type dependencies

Test-time efficiency claims need qualification: 4× savings analyzed only vs. majority voting; comparison to other adaptive sampling methods (early-stopping self-consistency) would strengthen claims; Figure 3 evaluates only two aggregation methods

strengths: Addresses a practically important problem: confidence calibration in search-augmented LLMs is critical for trustworthiness
Comprehensive experimental scope across 5 benchmarks and multiple model scales with thoughtful controlled ablations (Section 3.6)
Clear technical presentation of constrained RL formulation, well-grounded in prior work with detailed hyperparameters and computational requirements
Practical efficiency contribution: confidence-weighted aggregation matches 16-sample majority voting with 4 samples on 72B model
Transparent case study (Figure 4) effectively illustrates learned verification behaviors and confidence trajectories
weaknesses: Critical accuracy-calibration trade-off inadequately addressed: 7B model achieves only 0.35 average accuracy (vs. 0.55 for Claude Sonnet 4), suggesting false-certain rate reduction may reflect low overall confidence rather than genuine calibration improvement

Evaluation methodology significantly limited: uses oversimplified binary reliability metric (Eq. 5, threshold ζ=5) instead of proper calibration measures (ECE, calibration curves); no confidence score distributions or calibration curves reported; potential bias from using Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct as sole judge model

Limited technical novelty: core contribution is applying existing techniques (Paternain et al. 2023, GRPO from Shao et al. 2024, confidence-weighted voting from Taubenfeld et al. 2025) to search-augmented reasoning, not methodological innovation

Incomplete ablation and comparison: no comparison to simpler baselines (fixed-weight RLHF, temperature scaling) or other calibration methods cited but not evaluated; controlled ablation only compares to untrained baselines, not unconstrained RL variant

Confidence-weighted aggregation results overclaimed: comparison assumes confidence is calibrated (unverified), measures on same models lack independence, 4× efficiency depends on specific accuracy threshold with no sensitivity analysis

Out-of-distribution claims misleading: OOD accuracy extremely low (0.15-0.35 for 7B, 0.35 for 72B), making 'genuine uncertainty awareness' claims weak—difficult to distinguish principled calibration from expected uncertainty on harder tasks
Reproducibility barriers: requires 8-64 A100 GPUs for 20-60 hours; frozen LLM verifier unspecified; baseline training procedures not detailed; no random seed variance analysis
Missing critical ablations: no sensitivity analysis on reliability threshold ζ, Lagrange learning rate η=0.1, or initial multiplier λ₀=0.01; no justification for hyperparameter choices

Presentation issues: duplicate 'Figure 1' labels, reliability metric not fully explained until page 5, missing confidence score distributions and calibration visualizations essential for assessing calibration quality
No theoretical justification: limited explanation for why constrained RL improves calibration; strong duality conditions not rigorously verified in this setting

strengths: Clear, well-motivated problem addressing critical reliability issues in LLM deployment; the false-certain error mode is practically important and often overlooked
Principled and sound technical approach using constrained RL theory with adaptive Lagrangian multipliers, cleanly extending GRPO for joint correctness-reliability optimization
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 5 benchmarks (3 in-distribution, 2 OOD) with multiple model scales and strict controlled conditions using identical search tools

Rigorous ablation studies, particularly Table 2 isolating calibration learning from retrieval quality (untrained 72B shows 40%+ false-certain rates with same documents) and Appendix E demonstrating necessity of adaptive constraints

Dramatic empirical improvements: 96% reduction in false-certain rates (54%→2%) while maintaining/improving accuracy, demonstrating genuine uncertainty learning rather than memorization (wider reliability gap on OOD data)
Practical test-time compute efficiency gains (4× savings matching 16-sample majority voting with 4 samples) with immediate deployment value
Strong reproducibility with detailed hyperparameters, computational resources (20-60 GPU hours), complete training/evaluation prompts, and implementation details
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (established constrained RL, standard agent search, confidence calibration) without introducing new principles or theoretical insights

Reliability metric is overly simplistic with unjustified design choices: binary thresholding at ζ=5 lacks justification, and critically, no Expected Calibration Error (ECE) or standard calibration metrics reported, making it difficult to assess true calibration quality beyond false-certain reduction
Intermediate step-wise confidence scores are not optimized, despite being generated; only final answer confidence is in training objective—a missed opportunity acknowledged but not addressed

Key design choices lack justification or ablation: discrete 0-10 confidence scale rationale unexplained, specific hyperparameters (Table 3) without sensitivity analysis, connection between discrete confidence and true probability not established

No standard calibration analysis provided: missing calibration curves (confidence vs. accuracy), no comparison with recent calibration methods (proper scoring rules, etc.), unclear if calibration is good across full confidence spectrum or just binary high/low

OOD performance raises interpretability concerns: very low absolute accuracy (15-35% on GAIA/xbench-deepsearch) makes it unclear whether model learned genuine uncertainty or became inappropriately conservative; reliability improvements are relative rather than absolute

Potential confound not fully explored: Table 2 uses identical documents but doesn't investigate whether training altered document processing strategies beyond confidence calibration, especially given 'enhanced information extraction' findings in Section 3.6
Missing statistical rigor: no error bars, confidence intervals, or multiple-run variance; high-stakes claims (96% improvement) lack significance testing or stability analysis across seeds

Limited generalization scope: evaluated exclusively on QA tasks; unclear if approach transfers to classification, generation, or other task types; confidence calibration may be specialized to multi-hop reasoning
Inference cost analysis incomplete: no per-sample cost discussion including search operations; only aggregation efficiency discussed, not total overhead; iterative search may be expensive

Contemporaneous baseline comparisons needed: recent methods (R1-Searcher, Search-R1, ReSearch) published simultaneously; unclear what novel value Deliberative Searcher adds if these also incorporate confidence; would strengthen claims
